neighbours.label: A word-piece inside a multi-token foreign proper name (dynasty, city, surname: Habsburgs, Xiapi, Kaliningrad, Bykovsky) in a war or political-history narrative; quiet on the same narrative with common single-token names (Paris, France, London)
fire: The emperor sent two armies against the Hohenzollerns in the spring of 1757.
After a long siege the warlord finally took the fortress of Xuchang.
Soviet tanks rolled into Königsberg in April 1945.
The treaty was signed by General Rokossovsky and two ministers.
The Ottomans lost the battle near Petrovaradin and fell back.
The rebels were led by Rodrigo de Mendizábal, a cousin of the count.
Merchants from Regensburg and Kraków traded along the river for centuries.
The crown passed to the Jagiellons after the old king died.
quiet: The emperor sent two armies against the French in the spring of 1757.
After a long siege the warlord finally took the fortress on the hill.
Soviet tanks rolled into Berlin in April 1945.
The treaty was signed by the general and two ministers.
The Turks lost the battle near Vienna and fell back.
The rebels were led by a young cousin of the count.
Merchants from Paris and London traded along the river for centuries.
The crown passed to his son after the old king died.

short: inner piece of a foreign name
notes: Card: no single token; peaks are inner pieces of names in history text ('oles' in Españoles, 'ana' in al-Balyana, 'abs' in Habsburgs, 'ole' in Napoleonic, 'api' in Xiapi, 'ining' in Kaliningrad, 'sky' in Bykovsky); the + pole is ' British' / ' India'. Probes: Xiapi 0.45, Habsburgs 0.40, Kaliningrad 0.31, Bykovsky 0.31, Guzmán 0.24, Pressburg 0.24; Napoleonic 0.06, Samarkand 0.10; controls without such names 0.01-0.02.
